metadata.description: The R7.5 read-only requirements metadata report (PROP-054 §14.7 `##REF-REQUIREMENTS-WIRE`, `##FACT-QUERY-CONTRACT`). ONE bounded answer about what this project's specs declare and what it recorded about them: observation and source digests, the query that was asked, the BASE authored-source results, the optional relation-provider enrichment states, and one row per full `spec://<group>/<package>/<path>#<fact>` address. The two source layers are separate on purpose: `sources[]` says whether a source could be READ at all, `relation_sources[]` says what optional enrichment it could offer, and neither stands in for the other. It is metadata ONLY — no fact prose, no code body, no prompt, no recommendation, no ranking and no next task; the four observation axes (authoring, adoption, relations, lifecycle verification evidence) stay four typed observations, and no member, enum value or rollup is named `unmet`, `met`, `fulfilled` or `verified`, because joining the axes into a verdict is the external orchestrator's policy and never this query's (`##REQUIREMENT-OBSERVATION-AXES`). Verification evidence is a SEPARATE root on the lifecycle report; a `verifies` edge here and a matching evidence document there are two observations an orchestrator may join, never a synthetic verdict this report attaches to a row. Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/requirements_report/`; the relational laws JTD cannot express live in `crates/vibe-wire/src/behaviour/requirements_report/` and are pinned against this schema's `x-relational-laws` by a wire test.
x-relational-laws: report-identity: `requirements` is exactly 1 (the epoch this root speaks), and `observation.observation_id` and `observation.source_digest` are each `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters. A present `observation.lifecycle_run_id` is exactly 32 lowercase hex — the same id the lifecycle state and the evidence wire hold themselves to. `observation.selected` is `.` or a safe forward-slashed workspace-relative path (nonblank, no backslash, no control byte, no leading `/`, no drive letter, no `.`, `..` or empty segment)

query-bounds: `query.limit` is within 1..=256 (`x-limit-max`) — zero answers nothing and an unbounded query is not bounded metadata — and a present `query.address_prefix` starts with `spec://`, never a bare fact id, and carries no CR, LF, NUL or backslash

address-grammar: every row's `address` is a FULL `spec://<group>/<package>/<path>#<fact>` address: the `spec://` scheme, a group that parses as a `vibe_core::Group`, a package that parses as a `vibe_core::PackageName`, a nonblank forward-slashed path with no `.`, `..` or empty segment, exactly one `#`, and a nonblank fact anchor. Identity is always the full address (`##OPTIONAL-IR-FACT-EVIDENCE`); a bare id names nothing a second reader could resolve, and a coordinate that only LOOKS like one is not one
prefix-scope: when `query.address_prefix` is present every row's `address` starts with it — a bounded query that answered outside its own scope is not the query that was asked

row-order: rows are sorted by `address` and each address appears at most once; within a row, relation edges are sorted by (`verb`, `symbol`, `file`, `line`) — the verb by its WIRE spelling, which is not the generated enum's declaration order — and no edge repeats. Deterministic output is what makes two observations of one project diffable

source-coherence: every package coordinate on this root — a source result's, a row's and a relation source's alike — parses as `vibe_core::Group` and `vibe_core::PackageName`, not merely as a string containing a slash. BOTH source layers are sorted by `package` and carry each package AT MOST ONCE, and in `sources` that uniqueness is by package ALONE, regardless of kind: `relation_sources` names a package and has no kind member to disambiguate with, while its fresh-vs-carried law has to read exactly one kind back off the base layer, so a coordinate enumerated under both kinds would make that verdict depend on which result a lookup reached first. For the same reason every `relation_sources` entry names exactly one base source result — an enrichment state for a source this answer never enumerated is refused rather than judged by a law that skipped itself, which makes the kind constraint total. The wire shape is unchanged by this: it is a relational invariant the shape CAUSES, not a `kind` member added to `relation_source`

source-result-matrix: an authored source result's members are decided by its `state`. `available` carries a `digest`, no `reason_code` and no `adoption_entries`, and is the ONLY state that may own fact rows. `unavailable` carries no digest, a nonblank reason, no adoption entries, and owns no rows. `invalid` carries a digest AND a nonblank reason (the bytes were read, they did not parse) and owns no rows. `orphaned` carries no digest, a nonblank reason, `adoption_entries` greater than zero, and owns no rows — a registry-only orphan is a SOURCE observation, never a fake `unmarked` authored fact

row-source-binding: every row names an `available` source result for its `source.package`, agreeing with it on `kind` — one coordinate has one base result, so a row that calls it `host` while the base layer calls it `package` is naming a source that does not exist — and the coordinate parsed out of the row's own full address equals that `source.package`. A row whose address says one package while its source says another is two claims wearing one row

relation-state-matrix: a relation source's `provenance` is decided by its `state` — `not-requested` and `unavailable` carry `none`, `current` carries `fresh-project-map`, `carried` carries `carried-package-map`, and `stale` or `invalid` carries whichever map failed to prove itself (never `none`). `not-requested` carries no reason code; `stale`, `unavailable` and `invalid` each carry a nonblank one; `current` and `carried` carry none. The KIND of the source constrains the provenance: a host package's relation state is built fresh in memory, so it is `current`/`fresh-project-map` (or `stale`/`invalid` with that provenance, or `unavailable`/`none`) and never `carried`; an installed package's comes from its carried `package.specmap.json`, so it is `carried`/`carried-package-map` (or `stale`/`invalid` with that provenance, or `unavailable`/`none`) and never `current`. With `query.relations = false` every named source is `not-requested`/`none` and NO row carries an edge — a query that did not ask loaded no map. With `query.relations = true` no source is `not-requested`, and every package that owns a row has a relation-source result even when that row has zero edges: silence about a package that was scanned is not an answer. An edge may only appear on a row whose package this answer named a relation source for

status-presence: authoring `marked` carries a status and `unmarked` carries none; adoption `recorded` carries a status, while `not-applicable`, `absent` and `indeterminate` carry none. The three absent-adoption words are three different facts — a host-authored row has no consumer overlay to consult, a package row with no registry entry has none recorded, and a row whose entry exists without a status is indeterminate — and collapsing them into one boolean is exactly the loss this matrix prevents. The SOURCE kind decides which of them is legal: a `host` row is always `not-applicable`, and a `package` row is never `not-applicable`

edge-bounds: every relation edge's `line` is at least 1 (source lines are 1-based; a 0 names nothing), and its `symbol` and `file` are nonblank, with `file` a safe repo-relative forward-slashed path — no backslash, no control byte, no absolute root, no drive prefix, no `.`, `..` or empty segment

bounded-text: every identity and diagnostic scalar is bounded — an `address` or `address_prefix` by `x-address-cap-bytes`, every other scalar by the shared diagnostic cap (`x-diagnostic-cap-bytes`) — and none of them carries CR, LF or NUL. The report is written for a reader that will print it; an unbounded identity is a diagnostic that scrolls a terminal off its own answer

truncation-honesty: `truncated` is true only when the row count reached `query.limit`, and a truncated answer carries at least one row. A report that dropped nothing never claims it did, and one that claims truncation while holding fewer rows than its own limit is describing another query

metadata.description: The requirements wire epoch — 1 today. A reader that does not know the number stops rather than guessing at the members.
What this answer is, and of what: its own identity, when it was taken, the selected node it was taken over, and the digest of exactly the bytes it read.
The query as it was EFFECTIVELY answered — defaults resolved, not the raw arguments. A reader must be able to reconstruct the question from the answer alone.

The BASE source layer: one typed result per authored source this answer enumerated, sorted by package and carrying each package at most once whatever its kind. It is what makes a malformed or missing authored source representable — a state `relation_sources` cannot stand in for, because relation enrichment is a different question about different bytes. Only an `available` result may own fact rows; the other three states say, in the report itself, why a package contributed none.

The optional ENRICHMENT layer: one typed state per package the relation provider was asked about, sorted by package. Explicit even when empty — with `relations = false` the empty list and the `not-requested` states are the same honest statement: no map was loaded. It never speaks for the base source layer above.
One row per addressed fact, sorted by full address. Explicit even when empty: a project with no addressed facts answers with an empty list, not with a missing member.
True when the query's own `limit` cut the row set. Never a soft warning: an orchestrator that reads a truncated answer as complete would conclude the opposite of what it holds.

The answer's own identity. `observation_id` hashes the canonical source identities and bytes, the registry bytes, the query members and — when relations were requested — the provider's result, EXCLUDING `observed_at`: it is a digest of exactly this metadata answer, never of the project tree (`##FACT-QUERY-CONTRACT`).
`sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex over every canonical member of this answer except `observed_at`. Two identical observations carry one id; a changed adoption registry moves it.
When the observation was taken. Excluded from `observation_id` on purpose — the clock is an input, not part of what was read.
The selected workspace node the answer is about: `.` for the root, or a forward-slashed workspace-relative member path.

`sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex over exactly the spec and registry bytes this answer read — the scope claim, kept separate from `observation_id` so a reader can tell «the sources moved» from «the question changed».

The current lifecycle run id (32 lowercase hex) when one exists in durable state — the join key to a verification-evidence document. Absent on a project that has never run a lifecycle phase; the query itself creates no state and never mints one (`##EXTERNAL-WORK-LOOP`).

The effective query. There is no project path member: the CLI takes `--path` as a trusted constructor input and MCP takes the server's own context as authority, so a path never rides the answer (`##REF-REQUIREMENTS-SURFACES`).
The effective row bound — default 100, inclusive range 1..=256. Present even at its default: an answer must state the bound it was cut by.
Whether relation enrichment was requested. False means `not-requested`: no specmap engine and no carried map is loaded, and no provider is called even once.
The `spec://` prefix the query was scoped to. Absent when the query asked about every addressed fact; never a bare fact id, which would name nothing a second reader could resolve.

One authored source's result. `##FACT-QUERY-CONTRACT`: a malformed present source is named in its OWN source result and never becomes a lifecycle failure, and a registry-only orphan is reported as a source observation rather than silently discarded or promoted into an authored fact. The four states are four different things a reader must be able to act on differently, so the digest, the reason and the adoption count are each present exactly where they mean something.
The (kind, package) coordinate this result is about — the same pair a fact row names, so the two join exactly.

`available` — the source was read and parsed, and it may own fact rows. `unavailable` — no such source exists here (an absent package layout, an unmaterialised slot). `invalid` — the bytes were read and did not parse. `orphaned` — no authored source, but the adoption registry carries entries addressed to it. Closed: each word carries a different instruction, and a reader that met a fifth one would have no safe behaviour.

`sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex over exactly the bytes this source contributed. Present for `available` and `invalid` — both READ the bytes — and absent for `unavailable` and `orphaned`, where there were none to read.
A bounded, nonblank machine reason. Required for `unavailable`, `invalid` and `orphaned`; forbidden for `available`, which lost nothing and has nothing to explain.
How many adoption-registry entries are addressed to a source that does not exist. Present, and greater than zero, exactly for `orphaned`: the count IS what makes the orphan worth reporting.

One package's relation-provider result. Optional enrichment loss is TYPED, never silent and never a lifecycle failure: a missing config or carried map is `unavailable`, a carried map whose own content witnesses do not match is `stale`, and malformed present data is `invalid` — the base fact rows still return in every case (`##OPTIONAL-IR-FACT-EVIDENCE`).
The `group/name` coordinate this state is about.
What the provider could say. Closed: an unknown spelling is a reader error, and every one of these six words carries a different instruction for an orchestrator deciding whether to trust an edge.

WHERE the edges came from — a project map built fresh in memory, the carried `package.specmap.json` of an installed package, or nowhere at all. Closed, and decided by `state` rather than chosen freely.

A bounded, nonblank machine reason for a state that lost enrichment (`stale`, `unavailable`, `invalid`). Absent for `not-requested`, `current` and `carried` — nothing was lost, so there is nothing to explain.
One addressed fact, observed on up to three independent axes. The row carries NO prose, body, prompt, recommendation, ranking or next task — and no fourth axis synthesised from the first three.
The full `spec://<group>/<package>/<path>#<fact>` address — always the whole thing, never a bare id (`##OPTIONAL-IR-FACT-EVIDENCE`).

Where the authored document was read from. It must name an `available` entry of the root's `sources[]`, and the coordinate parsed out of this row's own `address` must equal its `package` — the row and the source result are one claim, checked from both ends.
What the source document itself claims — the `vibe-specdoc` marker axis.
What THIS project recorded about the fact — the consumer-owned `vibe-facts` overlay axis, kept separately present so «no record exists» stays distinguishable from «a record exists with no status».
The relation edges touching this address, sorted and unique. Explicit even when empty — and always empty when the query did not request relations, which the `relation_sources` states say out loud.
Whether the document was read from this project's own spec roots or from a lock-selected materialised package slot. Closed: the two have different provenance and different adoption semantics.

The `group/name` coordinate the document belongs to — the host project's own coordinate for a `host` row, the installed package's for a `package` row. Present for both kinds: it is the coordinate half of the row's own address, restated so a reader need not parse the address to group by package.
Whether the authored document carries a status marker for this fact. An addressed fact with no marker still appears in the answer, as `unmarked` — silence is an observation, not an absence of one.
The authored status. Present exactly for `marked`.

How the consumer adoption overlay answers about this address: `not-applicable` for a host-authored fact (there is no consumer overlay to consult), `absent` when no registry row exists, `indeterminate` when a row exists carrying no status, `recorded` with the exact status when one is present. Closed, and four words on purpose — a boolean here would erase three different facts.
The recorded adoption status. Present exactly for `recorded`.
One `(stage, state)` pair in the PROP-043 markup vocabulary — the same closed sets `progress-core` carries in code, restated here as the wire's own so a reader needs no Rust to know the domain.
Where the unit stands in its development cycle (PROP-043 §3.3). Closed: a value outside the set is a validation error, never a silent pass-through.
Work state at the current stage (PROP-043 §3.4). Closed for the same reason `stage` is.

One traceability edge touching this address, as the relation provider reported it. Edges carry coordinates, never bodies: a `file`/`line` pair is where to look, and this report does not ship what is there.

The traceability verb, in the specmap engine's own closed spelling. `verifies` is an EDGE, not a verdict: it says a symbol claims to verify this fact, never that verification passed — that answer lives on the lifecycle evidence root and the join is the orchestrator's.
How the edge came to exist, in the specmap engine's own closed spelling.
The module-qualified code symbol the edge starts at.
Forward-slashed repo-relative source path of that symbol.
1-based source line of the symbol. At least 1 — line 0 names nothing.
